newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Revised Australia trend job data corrected for phone effect.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Revised Australia trend job data corrected for phone effect.

text.p: A revised method of correcting Australian jobs data for the effect of telephone interviewing produces stronger full-time employment growth at the expense of part-time.
Australian Bureau of Statistics officials encourage private correction of the jobs data to exclude the effect, since they say the bureau will never adjust the published data itself.

The bureau says the introduction of telephone interviewing temporarily distorted its labour force data, depressing published growth rates until November and boosting those in December, January and February.
An initial set of corrected data, prepared with the assistance of the bureau, was published on Thursday under the headline "Corrected trend shows Australian jobs flat".
Bureau officials now suggest a better method of distributing the jobs effect between full and part-time workers.
The previous method applied the effect in proportion to growth rates. This greatly exaggerated recent divergence between full and part-time growth rates.
The data below instead distributes the effect simply in proportion to the full and part-time shares of employment levels, not growth.
